My fellow concerned American, I was one of the first savagely beaten by lawless, violent Antifa thugs.And unless we do something to stop them today, I won’t be the last. **[I’m asking you to donate $35 or more today to help me bring Antifa and its members who assaulted me to justice.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z683i6bgonif64tsfbdl2qq9ov5kp2seglovqsa8_rp22sh2s8i6eor4cdgeeo36cdh2bs) ****I was at Antifa's "ground zero" in Portland, Oregon during the summer of 2019.** This was before most Americans had ever heard of the Antifa movement, but they'd caused havoc and violence before.I went to an Antifa "protest" as a journalist to document and report on their “protest.”As soon as I arrived, I feared for my safety.The mob was angry, and violence always follows Antifa. Most of them wore masks to prevent being identified when they commit crimes. Many had on helmets and carried riot gear. Some, I later learned, secretly had weapons like baseball bats, brass knuckles and even bricks.I was scared, but I had a job to do, so I pressed on.**People like you needed to know what was happening.** But I didn't go unnoticed for long.Somebody recognized me and bashed me on the back of my head in an ambush."F*** you, Andy Ngo!" shouted voices around me. "Go home, fascist!"**Fists started flying at my face and head. Then came the projectiles.** Before I knew it, I was being repeatedly punched, kicked, and hit with objects.I tried to protect my head. I did not strike back as I knew that would only escalate the situation and put me in more danger.The thugs robbed me of my camera so that I wouldn’t have evidence of the assault. What they did to me is unacceptable and criminal. And now they're trying to do the same to other innocent Americans like you.That's why I sued members of the Rose City Antifa organization to bring them to justice and send the loud clear message that they are NOT above the law.Now I need your help to hold their feet to the fire and make sure justice is served. [**Will you donate $35 or more to help me hold Antifa accountable?**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zcc1qhrnmp2jot0rln38mb87be3s8d2c7mckjak0_rp22sh2s8i6eor4cdgeeo36cdh2bs) This is bigger than me alone. After I got away from the mob, police finally showed up when I was in the hospital. But my attackers stole my evidence and nearly silenced me permanently with a traumatic brain injury.Later, cell phone footage from a bystander surfaced online. Thank goodness! The video captured part of the attack, clear as day.I hoped I'd get the justice I deserved.Wrong.To this day, six years later, the Portland Police have done nothing.**No charges. No arrests. No suspects questioned.** It's not much of a surprise, though.Radical politicians have long since bowed to the dangerous left-wing mobs that terrorize their streets. That’s why the Center for American Liberty helped me file a lawsuit against my attackers. A judge ordered three of them to pay damages – but more than a year later and they have not paid a dime.So now the Center for American Liberty is helping me track them down and make them pay for nearly killing me and trampling upon the First Amendment.Unfortunately it’s going to cost at least $20,000 to get justice.[**That's why I hope you'll join the fight by donating $35 or more to fund my efforts to hold Antifa and its members accountable.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zdrrohdeiucpdk8lmjf917qp6rdlbhk8rqlctefg_rp22sh2s8i6eor4cdgeeo36cdh2bs) We have to stop Antifa and make them face real, legal consequences for their destructive actions before they get to you and your family.Antifa wants the literal end of America -- and they'll stop at nothing to get it. Believe me when I say that's not an overstatement. Some members are avowed socialists or communists. But many are much worse – open violent anarchists who want to tear down civilization and remake it in their own twisted vision with no law and order.By any means necessary.**_Rioting. Destruction. Mayhem._** And they know, as long as they choose politically favored protests to co-opt, the media and politicians will never have the guts to denounce their violence or hold them accountable. They did that with BLM. They’re doing it now against ICE.It's a sick strategy, but very smart – because so far, they've been successful.**For the most part, they've gotten off scot-free.** Our politicians and media are treating this terrorist group like peaceful protestors!As we saw in Los Angeles earlier this summer, their riots will only spread and intensify if Antifa continue to escape consequences.**So now I'm taking justice into my own hands – with the help of the talented lawyers at the Center for American Liberty.**

[**You can be a part of bringing Antifa to justice with a donation of $35 or more today.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zckh1efauvopkdilsu9ivnu067pqpdfqoea5874g_rp22sh2s8i6eor4cdgeeo36cdh2bs) Though I'm seeking justice for myself, the impact of this case could be so much larger.This is about standing up for our country when our own leaders won't.This is about saving America as we know it and keeping you and your family safe.And this is just the first blow we intend to deliver.By taking them to court for the attack against me we can prove they are NOT untouchable. **[Can I count on you to donate $35 or more to help me get justice from Antifa?](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z7pgs2i3hegpm8rm6dha4tvlq4u27n504deaasr0_rp22sh2s8i6eor4cdgeeo36cdh2bs) **Please don't wait – if we don't fight back and win now, **these violent thugs will be in EVERY city across America** , destroying everything and everyone in their path. Thank you in advance for your support.

Dear Peter,
The U.S. Department of Agriculture just confirmed what millions of families feared: **SNAP benefits will not go out on November 1.** That means 42 million Americans —working families already fighting hunger and poverty — are about to lose the modest assistance that keeps food on their tables. The USDA’s message was blunt: “The well has run dry.”While Donald Trump and Republican leaders build ballrooms and bail out Argentina with $40 billion, 42 million children, parents, seniors, and veterans are being abandoned — stressed out and scrambling about how to get food on their tables. **This is shameful, inhumane cruelty.****I am running for Congress because I believe government should feed families, not fuel chaos.** I’m fighting for accountability, compassion, and common sense — values that should never be up for debate.[**I know dollars are scarce now more than ever — but if you can help put sanity back in Congress, join me by donating $5 today.**](https://chrisahuja.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=97f443092fb7c091746070aa0&id=a6764105ed&e=5a6ee82cdb) Every contribution helps us reach more voters and fight for leadership that puts people first.Will you chip in whatever you can today to help me stand up for America’s most vulnerable?

subject: NYC is a symbol of our great nation
body:
We need to protect her at all costs.

| | | [](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zkgl46k02ghbaln9dv181id8mm42n00tupms3jso_rp22sh2s8i6eor4cdgeep74c5h2bs)
---
| | Republicans have a **once-in-a-lifetime opportunity** here in New York. With Zohran Mamdani and Andrew Cuomo splitting liberal voters, Republicans are primed for victory. New York has been on the backslide for years now with rising crime, failing schools, the highest cost of living in the country, and incompetent leadership in the Mayor's office. **Maybe it's time to give Republicans a chance to clean things up and _HUMILIATE_ the Democrats by beating them in a race they took for granted.**
---
[ HELP CURTIS PULL OFF AN UPSET WIN IN NYC! ](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zoknvraordfodkt6oq5d7jn1c1nvpu0436dt9ha0_rp22sh2s8i6eor4cdgeep74c5h2bs)
---
[](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2z02hl31ec0gruhddo06f74325q4t7e474llbcet8_rp22sh2s8i6eor4cdgeep74c5h2bs)
---
**New York City has always been symbolic of our great nation and the American Dream. ** But now she's at a crossroads. Zohran Mamdani wants to destroy our great city with his Socialist Agenda, increasing crime and taxing everyone into poverty. Republican candidate Curtis Sliwa doesn't just talk a big game - he walks it. **New Yorkers know Sliwa, and he has their trust.** He is a renowned community leader, activist, broadcaster and founder of the Guardian Angels - a famous volunteer civilian patrol that prevented crime and promoted safety on New York subways at a time when crime was out of control.

Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
folks,
Voting isn't a "one size fits all" activity. Forcing one method of participation only drives potential voters away, which is why we support a "yes, and" approach to casting your ballot. Here's how this works:
Can someone vote in person on Election Day? Yes, and they can also complete a ballot at home and mail it back. Are there other ways to participate? Yes, and they can drop that home ballot in a secure drop box, and they could vote early instead, and we can make Election Day a holiday to free more people to go vote... you get the idea. Simply put, the more ways we can make it easy for voters to participate, the more people who will make their voice heard by voting.
One of those methods -- early voting -- is open in many states with elections coming up. When Americans vote early, they ensure that nothing – not last minute problems, confusing election laws, long lines, or voter disinformation – can stop us from voting and making our voice heard.
Our mission is simple: The more people who vote, the more our government looks like what we, the people, want it to be. But to reach these voters and get them involved, we need your help .

It is a single day. That anyone might insist otherwise is difficult to imagine.

Last week, the Supreme Court heard oral arguments in Bost v. clean_body: If I’ve called you recently and you heard some unexpected crowing in the background...that was probably my rooster. | = | Hi Peter, If I’ve called you recently and you heard some unexpected crowing in the background...that was probably my rooster. Yes, I have chickens! They’re loud, funny, and endlessly curious. And honestly, when the world feels overwhelming, taking a few minutes to go outside and feed my chickens or collect their eggs helps me reset. = It’s grounding. It reminds me of what I’m fighting for: a more peaceful, fair, and decent world for all of us, not just the privileged few. But while the chickens can calm my nerves, they can’t power a campaign. clean_body: | | | Hi Peter, As we close out the month, I want to take a moment to reflect on what’s at stake and what’s possible. Donald Trump and his allies are attacking blue-state economies across the country — and Colorado is one of their first targets. I’ve spent my career fighting for transparency, fairness, and fiscal responsibility — values that ensure your tax dollars work for you, not for special interests. As your next State Treasurer, I’ll stand up to these attacks and fight to protect Colorado’s economy and save hardworking Coloradans money. I know what it means to work hard and make every dollar count. From watching my Italian immigrant grandparents run their small business, to my father leading his labor union, to holding my first job at 14 — I’ve seen the value of hard work my whole life. I’m running to ensure our state’s resources work for the hardworking people, not for right-wing politics or corporate special interests. Peter, When you run for office, you know you’re going to hear from plenty of folks who don’t agree with you. Trust me, I’ve caught plenty of flak from voters over the years. But that’s part of the job. As an elected official in a democracy, your job is to serve the people. That means you have to face voters directly and defend your policy choices. And if they don’t agree with you? Well, you just might get voted out of office. **That’s democracy. It’s how the system is supposed to work.** But right now, Republicans across the country, in lockstep with the White House, want to break that system. They have increasingly recognized that their ideas won’t sell, so they’re trying to rig the game, by drawing maps that splinter Democratic voting blocs or pack Democrats into just one district so that they don’t have influence in other districts. By redrawing electoral maps in states like Texas and Missouri in the middle of the decade, they’re trying to rewrite the rules of the game so they can’t lose. They want an America where politicians can pick their voters — rather than voters picking their politicians. **Eric Holder and I founded the National Democratic Redistricting Committee to push back on these extreme partisan power grabs that put our democracy in peril.[Can we count on you to stand with us and support this cause with a donation right now?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/118172143/578892258/-364004837?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_OctObama_email_20251028-NDRC-Tier1-OctObama_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20251028-NDRC-Tier1-OctObama_&utm_campaign=OctObama&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI3YmY0ZjIyLTJjYjQtZjAxMS04ZTYxLTYwNDViZGVkOGJhNCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=AQCNVkic3iSFfheCJ0q1ZfJXnvpXu6mwHINura0Ldqg=)** | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

Here’s the bigger problem: More Republican-led states are vowing to follow Texas and Missouri’s lead, and are planning to manipulate their own maps to benefit the Republican Party. Legislatures in Ohio and Indiana are considering extreme partisan redistricting measures that would take away representation from entire communities. In Kansas, some legislators are openly scheming to eliminate the district of the only Democratic representative in the state’s delegation and one of the first Native American women ever elected to Congress.
And this anti-democracy effort to silence voters isn’t just taking place in state legislatures. This administration’s Department of Justice filed a brief with the U.S. Supreme Court, trying to significantly weaken the part of the Voting Rights Act that prohibits the dilution of minority voting power.
Let me be clear: These types of power grabs remind us that democracy is not a given. It requires us to fight for it — especially in moments like this.

clean_body: Republicans can’t win on their policies, so they are trying to dodge accountability instead. We can stop them. | Peter, When you run for office, you know you’re going to hear from plenty of folks who don’t agree with you. Trust me, I’ve caught plenty of flak from voters over the years. But that’s part of the job. As an elected official in a democracy, your job is to serve the people. That means you have to face voters directly and defend your policy choices. And if they don’t agree with you? Well, you just might get voted out of office. That’s democracy. It’s how the system is supposed to work. But right now, Republicans across the country, in lockstep with the White House, want to break that system. They have increasingly recognized that their ideas won’t sell, so they’re trying to rig the game, by drawing maps that splinter Democratic voting blocs or pack Democrats into just one district so that they don’t have influence in other districts. By redrawing electoral maps in states like Texas and Missouri in the middle of the decade, they’re trying to rewrite the rules of the game so they can’t lose. They want an America where politicians can pick their voters — rather than voters picking their politicians. Eric Holder and I founded the National Democratic Redistricting Committee to push back on these extreme partisan power grabs that put our democracy in peril.= | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = Here’s the bigger problem: More Republican-led states are vowing to follow Texas and Missouri’s lead, and are planning to manipulate their own maps to benefit the Republican Party. Legislatures in Ohio and Indiana are considering extreme partisan redistricting measures that would take away representation from entire communities. In Kansas, some legislators are openly scheming to eliminate the district of the only Democratic representative in the state’s delegation and one of the first Native American women ever elected to Congress. And this anti-democracy effort to silence voters isn’t just taking place in state legislatures. This administration’s Department of Justice filed a brief with the U.S. Supreme Court, trying to significantly weaken the part of the Voting Rights Act that prohibits the dilution of minority voting power. Let me be clear: These types of power grabs remind us that democracy is not a given. It requires us to fight for it — especially in moments like this. body:
Those polls showing a close race are real, and we’re responding.
#
Peter, we’ll get right to the point.
A recent Emerson poll found this race tied — with tons of undecided voters. It’s not an outlier. We’ve lost count of how many polls have come out in recent weeks showing this race functionally tied.
In a race this close, the last thing we can afford is for people who support Mikie Sherrill to not show up to the polls, or leave their mail-in ballot sitting on their kitchen table.

Fellow Patriot,
The Virginia governor’s race is razor-thin, with RealClearPolitics showing just a **3% difference** between the candidates in the latest poll. That margin could be as high as **95,700 votes** or as low as **82,800**. The difference between godly leadership and policies that ignore biblical values.

subject: The Mountain Minute: 10/28/2025
body:
How Colorado’s “Right to Know” built a hospital compliance registry
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** A new [Colorado Hospital Association report](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) found nearly 70% of hospitals ended 2024 on “unsustainable” margins, with rural facilities hit hardest by staffing shortages and Medicaid cuts. Meanwhile, an 18-year-old became the face of [Colorado’s healthcare ideology debate](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) after a late-night ER visit for a stomachache turned into a dispute over mandatory “Patients’ Right to Know” forms on abortion, gender care, and end-of-life policies.
In Aurora, police arrested a man [deported three times](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in connection with a shooting on I-225, reigniting frustration over weak federal immigration enforcement. In Colorado Springs, Rampart High senior Sophia Shumaker was barred from painting a Bible verse on her parking spot, [sparking debate over free speech](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and religious expression in public schools.
🇺🇸 **On the National Stage...** The [federal shutdown fight deepened](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as Colorado’s four Republican congress members—Jeff Crank, Lauren Boebert, Gabe Evans, and Jeff Hurd—pressed Democratic Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper to back a clean funding bill. [They warned the shutdown](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) has sidelined 55,000 federal workers, jeopardized food aid for 600,000 residents, and frozen $36 million in FEMA funds, costing Colorado nearly $289 million in GDP weekly. At the same time, an investigative report revealed that [a top U.S. teaching college](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) is embedding Marxist and socialist frameworks in its curriculum, fueling debate over ideological indoctrination and the erosion of neutrality in education.

🗣️ **Commentary Spotlight...** In Montrose County, Michael Badagliacco backs Neisha Balleck, Tiffany Vincent, Scott Scarborough, and Shane Daly—[candidates emphasizing parental rights](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), fiscal discipline, and academic focus over ideology. In Delta County, Angie Many supports Sheldon Kier and Adena Kreutz as [common sense reformers](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) committed to literacy and civics over activism. Nationally, a growing “campus right” movement is taking shape as Gen Z conservatives champion free expression and intellectual debate—[redefining how young Americans engage](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) with politics and culture.
This is the Mountain Minute for Tuesday, October 28, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[From stomachache to ideology: How Colorado’s “Right to Know” built a hospital compliance registry](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)

Just after midnight, an 18-year-old Colorado woman—identified here as “Clarity” to protect her identity—went to the ER, hoping the pain was only a severe case of gastritis. She’s a recent high-school graduate now working for a Colorado nonprofit and was granted anonymity by RMV. When Clarity was finally told she could leave, someone brought over an iPad and said she needed to finish a few discharge questions before going home.
On the screen was Colorado’s Patients’ Right to Know Act Service Availability Form—pages of items about gender-affirming care, abortion services and end-of-life options. “She was yelling at us over Zoom, saying, ‘Do you understand that you have access to these services and you’re knowingly denying them?’” Clarity recalled. “My mom said, ‘We don’t want to answer these questions.’ The lady said, ‘I can’t let you leave until you answer these questions.’ It was one in the morning—we just wanted to go home.”
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[School District Faces Backlash After Banning Bible Verse in Student Artwork](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [BIZPAC REVIEW](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Rampart High School senior Sophia Shumaker was prohibited from decorating her assigned parking spot with a Bible verse, which she had planned to paint as part of a senior tradition.
* The district cited policy restrictions on religious or political messaging on school property, though students are typically encouraged to personalize their spots with creative designs.
* The decision has sparked community backlash and debate over students’ First Amendment rights, religious expression, and school censorship in public education.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Hospitals on life support: Report says 70% of Colorado facilities losing money](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER GAZETTE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Nearly 70% of Colorado hospitals ended 2024 with “unsustainable” margins, as expenses have risen 52% since 2019 while revenue grew only 39%, according to the Colorado Hospital Association.
* Rural hospitals are in even greater financial distress, with over 80% unable to maintain solvency, leading to the closure of three behavioral health centers and the loss of roughly 500 jobs statewide.
* The report attributes the crisis to the Medicaid unwind, rising uncompensated care, and federal budget cuts projected to eliminate $10 billion in hospital funding over five years, threatening coverage for more than 100,000 Coloradans.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
** ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[The conservative candidates—Sheldon Kier and Adena Kreutz—are best for Delta Schools](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) **
**BY ANGIE MANY | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 27** _As Colorado mandates more and more laws affecting students and school districts, school board elections have become increasingly important. Unfortunately, despite the importance of electing members to guide school policies, such ‘off-year’ elections traditionally have poor voter turnout. ‘We the people’ need to start paying more attention and devoting a little time to learning more about the people who will have such an impact on the education – and the indoctrination – that our children receive. And then we need to vote._
**[Championing Conservative Principles: Balleck, Vincent, Scarborough, and Daly for Montrose County School Board](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY MICHAEL BADAGLIACCO | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 27** _With over 5,000 students across diverse rural and urban communities, the Montrose County School District is at a crossroads. Nationwide, school boards have become battlegrounds for competing visions of education, with too many leaning into divisive ideologies that undermine parental authority and academic rigor. On November 4, 2025, Montrose voters have a chance to steer our schools back to conservative principles by electing Neisha Balleck, Tiffany Vincent, Scott Scarborough, and Shane Daly to the School Board._
**[Rep. Hurd refuses pay, passes first bill and earns Trump endorsement in decisive week](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | OCTOBER 25** President Trump’s “Complete and Total Endorsement” of Congressman Jeff Hurd on Saturday capped a remarkable week for the freshman lawmaker from Colorado’s Third District. Trump praised Hurd‘s “strong Record of SUCCESS,” for “fighting tirelessly to... Advance American Energy DOMINANCE, Grow the Economy, Cut Taxes and Regulations...” and “HE WILL NOT LET YOU DOWN.”

**Feel like you have a unique story, commentary or tip to share?** Email [submit@rockymountainvoice.com](mailto:submit@rockymountainvoice.com).
|
---
|
---
**🧠 DID YOU KNOW?** **Did you know that if your school allows any non-academic clubs,** it legally [has to allow all viewpoints](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—religious, political, or otherwise? Federal law (20 U.S.C. § 4071) guarantees equal access for student groups, and the Supreme Court has ruled that denying recognition or funding based on beliefs counts as viewpoint discrimination.

| | Peter,

**What’s happening in Washington, D.C. isn’t just politics – it’s devastating our communities in Eastern Washington.**

We’re now on day 28 of the government shutdown because the party holding the White House and the majority in both houses of Congress has taken a _“my way or the highway”_ approach to draft legislation that requires a bipartisan supermajority in the Senate to pass into law.

**The House, including WA05’s own Rep. Baumgartner, has been on paid time off for most of the past four months. Meanwhile, some non-partisan public servants in essential jobs are working without pay.**

**And now, it’s about to get even scarier.** If the shutdown continues beyond Halloween, the USDA intends to withhold available contingency funding and suspend SNAP benefits, _the food aid program that puts meals on the table of more than 40 million Americans, and reliable income in the hands of family farmers, including here in WA05._

**You read that right: the money for SNAP is there, and could be available through a shutdown. **The administration is choosing to use hungry people as pawns. This isn’t leadership, it’s cruelty. Hundreds of thousands of Americans will lose access to food – seniors; veterans and military families; working families with children – in pursuit of an extreme agenda.

**We cannot stay silent.**[**We need to send a clear message to Michael Baumgartner right now: put Eastern Washington first, and insist the USDA fund the programs families rely on to stay fed and healthy, and farmers rely on to get their crops to local markets.**](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=6fc432be41&e=a7b299e420)
---
| **[SIGN ON](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=bfee1d7f39&e=a7b299e420)**
---
| | In Eastern Washington, 50,000 rely on SNAP to keep food on the table through the end of the month. SNAP also supports local farmers who sell their food and products to local markets. If those benefits stop, local folks suffer, and farmers lose critical income.

Michael Baumgartner has turned his back on the people he was elected to serve. His refusal to act means families will lose food assistance, healthcare, and the basic stability our communities deserve.

**Eastern Washington deserves better – and together, we can demand it.**

Thank you for speaking out today,

Carmela Conroy

But, Peter, this is not just about me. It’s about the dangerous precedent being set for our justice system – where any president can install their own prosecutor to punish their political rivals.
That’s not democracy. That’s authoritarianism.

body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1001&akid=1185%2E251025%2EDku5Mp ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1002&akid=1185%2E251025%2EDku5Mp ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter,

We just updated our Path to Victory Memo, and we wanted to share it with
you. It lays out where we’re gaining ground and what we’ll need to win
this race:

Abdul for U.S. Senate — Path to Victory Memo

State of the Race

Multiple election analysts rate Michigan as a toss-up, making it one of
the most competitive Senate races in the country. Whoever wins here could
determine majority control of the entire Senate.

Abdul has built one of the strongest progressive campaigns in the nation,
earning endorsements from Senator Bernie Sanders, Congressman Ro Khanna,
the Michigan Democratic Party Progressive Caucus, and dozens of local
leaders.

This early momentum makes it clear — our campaign has the energy and broad
support needed to win in both the primary and general elections.

Unpredictability

One of the biggest questions right now is whether or not the Michigan
state legislature will shift our primary date from August to May. If we
lose three critical months to campaign, we’ll have to accelerate our
operations on every front.

That means reaching more voters in a shorter time frame and squeezing more
events into our calendar — both of which require more financial resources.

Fundraising Update

In Q3, our campaign raised $1.77 million — more in individual
contributions than any other campaign in this race. (Corporate PACs don’t
count.)

Meanwhile, the primary opponent we’re neck-and-neck with in the polls is
bankrolled by AIPAC and corporate PACs.

Keeping up this fundraising pace is crucial, especially as AIPAC starts to
explicitly target our campaign.

As you can see, a major factor in winning this competitive primary is
whether or not we can generate enough grassroots momentum to reach
Michiganders across the state.

Here are a few ways to make a positive impact:

* [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/543?c0=em-ms-aes-20251028-1-ak.1zbRJl&amount=10&refcode=em20251028-1184&t=1004&akid=1185%2E251025%2EDku5Mp ]If you’re in a position to invest long-term, start a recurring
donation today. Being able to count on your support each month is an
incredible resource for our campaign.
* If you’re able to pitch in a few bucks today, [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20251028-1-ak.uxgJow&amount=10&refcode=em20251028-1184&t=1005&akid=1185%2E251025%2EDku5Mp ]you can make a
one-time contribution by clicking here. Individual contributions are
the lifeblood of this movement.
* If you can’t donate today, that’s fine too. Consider volunteering with
us! [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/signup/volunteer/?source=em20251028-1184&t=1006&akid=1185%2E251025%2EDku5Mp ]There are multiple ways to get involved — explore them by
clicking here.

Thanks so much,

Team Abdul

| When I talk about going to bat for working folks in Washington, it’s not lip service.
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/67?t=1&akid=5076%2E35263%2ENT-tSI)
[](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/2155?c0=stb-em-craig.XwkA4Y&refcode=AU_STB_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20251028_PM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=5076%2E35263%2ENT-tSI) Can I share something deeply personal with you, Peter? I was raised by a single mom in a mobile home park. My mom worked full-time and earned her teaching degree over the span of 9 years. My grandmother, who lived a few doors down, worked in a shoe factory well into her 70s — all while she helped my mom raise me and my two siblings. That’s where I come from. Nothing came easy. I got my first job at McDonald’s as a teenager and put myself through state college, working two jobs and taking out some student loans. I started off my career as a reporter and spent 20 years helping lead a major Minnesota manufacturing company, eventually leading a team of 16,000. **When I talk about going to bat for working folks in Washington, it’s not lip service. I’m talking about my mom, my grandmother, my aunts and uncles, my siblings and _everyone_ who knows what it’s like to struggle. I’m fighting for them, and I’m fighting for you.** Right now, Donald Trump and his GOP majority are making it nearly impossible for regular folks to make ends meet — and that’s got to change. **[So Peter, I’m humbly asking before my October deadline: Will you please split $10 between Tammy Baldwin and my campaign to send me to the U.S. Senate and chart a better path forward for working families?](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/2155?c0=stb-em-craig.XwkA4Y&refcode=AU_STB_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20251028_PM1_V1_S1&t=5&akid=5076%2E35263%2ENT-tSI)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation to Angie Craig and Tammy Baldwin will go through immediately:_ | | [CHIP IN $10 NOW](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/3664?c0=stb-em-craig.J6t6Ye&refcode=AU_STB_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20251028_PM1_V1_S1&t=6&akid=5076%2E35263%2ENT-tSI)

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. | | **Hurricane Melissa: A Call to Action for Jamaica**
---
|
---
|
---
---
| **Hurricane Melissa has officially intensified into a catastrophic Category 5 storm and is now impacting Jamaica with violent winds, destructive storm surge, and extreme rainfall.** Officials are urging residents to shelter in place, as massive flooding, landslides, and infrastructure failure are expected across the island. This is being reported as one of the strongest hurricanes ever recorded near Jamaica and is already causing widespread damage and life-threatening conditions. **Steve Slepcevic** , Founder & CEO of **Strategic Response Partners (SRP) and VP of Autism Health** , is currently in Jamaica working with critical facilities and local partners to prepare for rapid recovery after the storm clears. With more than three decades of disaster response experience, Steve and his team specialize in emergency logistics, business continuity, infrastructure assessments, and property recovery. Their work becomes essential in the aftermath — when families are displaced, businesses are shut down, and communities lose access to clean water, power, and shelter. If you feel called to support ongoing emergency efforts, please consider donating to assist recovery operations on the ground. Your contribution helps mobilize critical supplies, specialized equipment, and direct aid to families who may not have the resources to rebuild on their own. **Donate here:** [https://www.givesendgo.com/SRP](https://autismhealth.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7c0b21e245e40197b3670bea2&id=fb59ee1b50&e=3a42edfdc4). Please join me in praying for Steve’s safety and for the people of Jamaica as they face this historic storm. Climate-driven hurricane intensification continues to raise global concern — and moments like this remind us how deeply we depend on each other.

body:
Peter,

Republicans' reckless government shutdown has left working families in limbo.

Folks are going without their paychecks, small businesses are left waiting on contracts, and communities are waiting for help that should've come _yesterday._

And to make matters worse, Donald Trump just pulled nearly **$200 million** in federal funding for the St. Louis battery plant, a project that would've created _over 1,000 good-paying jobs right here in St. Louis._

That's not just a bad policy decision — **it's a slap in the face to St. Louis workers and families who've been counting on those jobs.** Wesley's been fighting tirelessly in Congress to reopen the government, protect healthcare subsidies, and make sure our region gets the investments we were promised.

But while he's pushing to get Washington working again, the GOP is playing political games that put real people at risk. Peter, as St. Louisans and millions of other Americans are left to deal with the GOP's partisan carnage, it's clear that this is a fight we simply can't afford to sit out. We have to hold Trump and his allies in Congress accountable and make sure St. Louis families come first, not partisan politics.

name: Steve Kerrigan
subject: One Week Until Municipal Election Day!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Massachusetts Democratic State Committee
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Logo.png]
Dear Peter,
One week from today, voters from dozens of cities and towns in Massachusetts will go to the polls. While municipal elections are non-partisan, we have an incredible opportunity to support candidates that reflect our priorities and values as Democrats.
Even if you don't normally vote in local races, please do so this year. We know that every vote, every campaign and every election matters. Make a plan to vote: in-person, early or absentee in next Tuesday's election.
If you live in a town that does not have an election on Tuesday, November 4, please consider volunteering in a nearby community that does, or sign up to volunteer to help elect Democrat Abigail Spanberger as Governor of Virginia and Mikie Sherrill as Governor of New Jersey.
Sign up to make phone calls into Virginia and New Jersey Here [https://www.mobilize.us/massdems/event/804092/]
We also encourage you to lend a hand in the efforts to protect absentee voting in Maine ( No on Question 1 ) and fair redistricting in California ( Prop 50 ).
Expanding access to the ballot is at the heart of our democracy and victories in these fights will help strengthen voting rights nationwide.
No on Question 1 (Phonebank) [https://www.mobilize.us/mainedems/event/855836/?referring_vol=6129474&rname=Alex&share_context=event_details&share_medium=copy_link]
No on Question 1 (Canvass) [https://www.mobilize.us/mainedems/event/855837/?referring_vol=6129474&rname=Alex&share_context=event_details&share_medium=copy_link]
Proposition 50 [https://www.mobilize.us/massdems/event/856571/]
If you’re able, consider signing up to volunteer or contribute to these efforts to ensure every eligible voter can make their voice heard.
As Massachusetts Democrats, we don't agonize...we organize. Please join our grassroots movement today.

clean_body: The cooking show that centers immigrant stories is BACK! | | | Hey Peter, Dust your aprons off! ** 🧑🍳✨ That's right! The new season of** Just Flavors!— our immigrant youth cook-off show – premieres on YouTube next week. Last season, you saw our contestants prepare their favorite family recipes and celebrate the stories behind them. This season, you’re in for a whole new line-up of contestants, guest stars, recipes, and empowering stories. Food, like people, tells incredibly powerful stories about our communities. It’s our reminder that, whether it's a shared meal at the table or a collective chant at a rally, our ability to unite across differences is what makes us powerful. 👉📺 Watch our new trailer today for a sneak peek into the delicious dishes coming to your screen on November 4: ** In a time when our communities are facing challenges to our safety and dignity, Just Flavors! is a celebration of our immigrant identities and an invitation to reclaim our stories and cultures. 🥘🧡 Let your friends know that Just Flavors! is back. There's a lot of campaign left, and we hope you'll stick with us and support us in these next steps! Thanks, Team Kat Abughazaleh 🐈 Friend, it's Kat Abughazaleh, and if this isn't a sign of what's to come, I don't know what is.

**_Donald Trump is planning on attacking payment processor ActBlue in another attempt by his administration to push the limits of his power._**
The detainment of Mahmoud Kahlil, the deportation of Kilmar Abrego Garcia, and the outright denial to follow a ruling made by the Supreme Court are all blatant oversteps that attack our right to free speech and due process and challenge the rule of law.
Friend, I've spent years watching Fox News and listening to their rhetoric get more and more extreme, and Donald Trump is doing exactly what they want.
**_Fascism is, and has always been, their end goal._**
Their vision is one of a militarized country where only certain people—a few dozen rich men—have a seat at the table, and dissidents like me are silenced.
Trump and Elon know that progressive movements like ours are in the way because I've made it abundantly clear that strongly worded letters, wearing matching outfits while holding up signs, and meaningless acts of symbolism **aren't my thing.**
As a member of Congress, I'm going to be unwavering in my fight for our communities.
I will not vote for authoritarian bills in the name of "compromise," I will not abandon or demonize vulnerable groups to cater to the right, and I will not change my stances for fear of retaliation.
And Friend, that's what this action on ActBlue is: retaliation. Campaigns like ours rely on small dollars from people like you to support us, and ActBlue is integral to making that work.

Not just any challenger either — a DNC member with powerful connections and the ability to fundraise against us.
**[If you understand the stakes of this race and want to be part of the movement to reelect Ilhan Omar, please rush a donation to our campaign right now >>](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-oct25.q9Ch2B&refcode=em251028-2-210&t=3&akid=1930%2E791427%2ERsDtpg)**

At a time when Donald Trump is on the war path, consolidating more power into his hands, sending troops into our cities, and punishing his political enemies, we need strong progressive leaders who know how to stand up and fight back.

name: Seth Moulton
subject: Some things are worth saying twice.
body:
I wanted to revisit my “why” because it’s the heart of this campaign.

| |
---
Hi friend, I shared this message when our campaign launched, but it feels more urgent now. I hope you’ll take another look. When people ask me why I’m running for the U.S. Senate, my answer always comes back to one thing: **taking action when it matters most.** After serving overseas, I came home determined to fix the broken politics that put lives at risk and left Washington paralyzed by caution and complacency. I learned firsthand what happens when leaders hesitate rather than act with courage and conviction. That’s why I ran for Congress. Not because it was easy, but because Massachusetts families deserved better than the same old politics and failed leadership. Ten years later, I’m running for Senate for the same reason: our country is in crisis, and the urgency of this moment demands change — not complacency. Washington is filled with career politicians who have spent decades in office while Donald Trump and his MAGA allies tear down our democracy, weaponize government, and turn Americans against one another at a breakneck speed. Meanwhile, too many Democrats are standing still. I'm not afraid to call out our party's weaknesses, friend. It’s time for a new generation of leaders, people who won’t accept “good enough” when families are hurting, who will meet this moment with courage, urgency, and a plan for the future. **That’s why I’m running for Senate:** To stand up to Trump and his enablers, to hold this administration accountable, and to fight for families struggling to pay the bills, veterans waiting for care, and kids growing up in a country that should not only inspire them to dream big, but set them up to make those dreams a reality. I’ve never been afraid to challenge the status quo, whether it was in the Marines, in Congress, or in my own party. Everybody playing nice and waiting their turn is how we've ended up where we are today. **This isn’t a time for caution. clean_body: I wanted to revisit my “why” because it’s the heart of this campaign. | | Hi friend, I shared this message when our campaign launched, but it feels more urgent now. I hope you’ll take another look. When people ask me why I’m running for the U.S. Senate, my answer always comes back to one thing: taking action when it matters most. After serving overseas, I came home determined to fix the broken politics that put lives at risk and left Washington paralyzed by caution and complacency. I learned firsthand what happens when leaders hesitate rather than act with courage and conviction. That’s why I ran for Congress. Not because it was easy, but because Massachusetts families deserved better than the same old politics and failed leadership. Ten years later, I’m running for Senate for the same reason: our country is in crisis, and the urgency of this moment demands change — not complacency. Washington is filled with career politicians who have spent decades in office while Donald Trump and his MAGA allies tear down our democracy, weaponize government, and turn Americans against one another at a breakneck speed. Meanwhile, too many Democrats are standing still. I'm not afraid to call out our party's weaknesses, friend. It’s time for a new generation of leaders, people who won’t accept “good enough” when families are hurting, who will meet this moment with courage, urgency, and a plan for the future. That’s why I’m running for Senate: To stand up to Trump and his enablers, to hold this administration accountable, and to fight for families struggling to pay the bills, veterans waiting for care, and kids growing up in a country that should not only inspire them to dream big, but set them up to make those dreams a reality. I’ve never been afraid to challenge the status quo, whether it was in the Marines, in Congress, or in my own party. Everybody playing nice and waiting their turn is how we've ended up where we are today. This isn’t a time for caution. It’s a time for change. This is my "why," friend. Across the country, folks are feeling the pinch as prices continue to rise.

| Hi Peter,

Across the country, folks are feeling the pinch as prices continue to rise.

| | |
---
Friend, families shouldn’t have to stress about child care. It should be high-quality, reliable, and within reach.

But right now, that’s just not the reality for too many families in Colorado.
**That's why I just rolled out my plan to make child care more affordable for Colorado's working families.**
**_[But to put it into action, I first need your help to reach my campaign's $5,000 end-of-month goal this Friday. **_Right now,_** child care for just _one_ infant costs Colorado families nearly $22,000 a year on average – the fifth most expensive nationwide.
**_Right now, _**we _also_ face a shortage of licensed child care providers, with only enough capacity to serve 20% of Colorado babies and toddlers.
**_Right now,_** most child care workers aren’t paid a living wage for the demanding and essential job they do.
And **_right now,_** Colorado loses out on ** $2.7 billion ** each year – since many parents who want to work have to stay home, because they can't find affordable child care.
Our current reality isn't just ridiculous – it's unacceptable.
[But with your help to win this race,](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/118181196/578919616/851209409?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk955-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMDUwNzI3Ni00MmI0LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Cql6qnoUCV6HNDsZPckI7BFxapYdgUhJbGUO9HyKhVo=) **I will do everything I can as governor to create opportunities for every family to find ****affordable, high-quality child care for every child in Colorado from birth to age 5** – and here's how:
When it comes to **lowering child care costs for families and expanding provider capacity,** I'm talking about starting a loan fund to help providers give affordable care to working families, strengthening the Colorado Child Care Assistance Program, offering tax incentives for small business owners starting and running new child care centers and empowering home-based providers with essential assistance and community resources.
When it comes to **ensuring child care workers receive the fair compensation and benefits they deserve,** I'm talking about supporting local efforts to subsidize wages, expanding access to affordable health insurance across the entire workforce, making Care Worker Tax Credits permanent and scaling programs that make it easier to become a child care worker.
And when it comes to **cutting the red tape that creates unintentional delays and costs without compromising quality,** I'm talking about a systematic overhaul of our state's licensing system, removing barriers to home-based care options and creating a locally driven, statewide portal and common app system that makes finding affordable child care easier.
This plan is guided by my belief that we all share a responsibility to look out for one another and for the next generation.
**But real progress for working families and future generations demands that we _all_ step up, and it has to start from the grassroots. That means I can't make any of this happen without you.**

Every contribution of $5, $25 or more ahead of my end-of-month deadline this Friday will help my campaign reach more of Colorado's workers and families – and together, I believe we can make Colorado the best place to live, work and raise a family.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/118181198/578919617/851209409?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk955-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMDUwNzI3Ni00MmI0LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Cql6qnoUCV6HNDsZPckI7BFxapYdgUhJbGUO9HyKhVo=)_ **

Thirteen times, fellow American...

Senate Democrats have voted _**thirteen times**_ against a bipartisan bill to fund and reopen the federal government, and there seems to be no end in sight.

_Why?_ Because they think they can afford to dig in.

After outraising Republicans in nearly every key Senate race last quarter, Democrats believe their hordes of campaign cash justify holding America hostage.

They think that their donors from New York and California can bankroll their shutdown antics and break our resolve.

They’re clinging to a radical agenda that prioritizes illegal immigrants over American families — and it’s the American People who are paying the price.

Senate Democrats have voted thirteen times against a bipartisan bill to fund and reopen the federal government, and there seems to be no end in sight. Why? After outraising Republicans in nearly every key Senate race last quarter, Democrats believe their hordes of campaign cash justify holding America hostage. They think that their donors from New York and California can bankroll their shutdown antics and break our resolve. They’re clinging to a radical agenda that prioritizes illegal immigrants over American families — and it’s the American People who are paying the price. It’s time to send a clear message to Democrats: End the Schumer Shutdown. Put America First. Democrats are clearly listening to their donor base and the hordes of campaign cash they raked in last quarter. There’s only one way they’ll get the message: Your loud support will not only pressure Democrats to end the shutdown now, but it will also go immediately toward our fight to strengthen our Senate majority so we don’t have to go through this again. name: AOTL
subject: This anti-democracy attack has been over a century in the making.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE NATIONAL REDISTRICTING ACTION FUND
body:
AOTL logo [https://nvlupin.blob.core.windows.net/images/van/EA/EA013/1/89296/images/email-theme/aotl-navy.png]

The redistricting case before the Supreme Court — Louisiana v. Callais — could decide the future of critical voting rights protections. And we at AOTL have to be ready to respond, so that we can empower voters, no matter what the Court may rule.

Let’s take a look at how we got here:

1869

The 15th Amendment was passed, affirming that the "right of citizens of the United States shall not be denied or abridged . . . on account of race." As a sponsor of the amendment said at the time, this guarantees Black voters the right to “choose from among his fellow citizens the man who suits him for his representative,” AKA, vote. The amendment also empowered Congress to pass laws to ensure its enforcement.

1883

Much of the enforcement of Reconstruction amendments — the rules to help ensure civil rights protections — was dismantled, weakening the federal government’s protections of voting rights.

1965

Civil Rights leaders passed the Voting Rights Act (VRA), enforcing strong protections for voters of color nationwide.

1982

Shortly after a U.S. Supreme Court decision interpreted the Voting Rights Act narrowly, in such a way as to make the law weaker, Congress quickly amended the statute to clarify its full power, significantly enhancing Section 2, which prohibits vote dilution against voters of color nationwide.

Section 2 means that maps cannot have the effect of denying groups of voters of color from electing their candidate of choice when they would otherwise have the power to do so. It is one of the most powerful tools for communities to ensure that courts can enforce their right to have a voice in their government.

2022

Louisiana drew a map that allowed Black voters to elect a candidate of their choice in just one of six congressional districts — despite the fact that Black voters make up a third of the state’s population. The fair maps movement successfully challenged this map in court, and the map was found by a federal district court to likely violate Section 2 of the VRA.

2023

The U.S. Supreme Court resoundingly reaffirmed the power of the Voting Rights Act, in Allen v. Milligan, a case arising from Alabama. Following the case, litigation in Louisiana, which had been on pause awaiting the Milligan decision, continued, and additional federal courts affirmed the substance of the lower court’s ruling against Louisiana’s map.

2024

Louisiana — now having had seven different federal judges agree that its previous map likely violates the Voting Rights Act — redrew its map. The new map drawn by the Louisiana legislature allowed Black voters to elect their candidate of choice in two districts, instead of only one.

2024-2025

Louisiana’s fair map was challenged by non-Black voters known as the Callais appellees, who argued that they were harmed by a map that allowed Black voters additional representation. The Supreme Court heard the case earlier this year, but instead of ruling, opted to hear the case for a second time this October.

Section 2 of the VRA is at stake — which could have nationwide implications for fair maps. If the court rules in favor of the Callais appellees, voters of color across the country could lose key protections.

Today

We have to be ready to respond. All of our progress for fair representation is on the line. With so much at stake, we have to be ready for whatever legal changes may come next. We have to empower the grassroots to fight back with information and tools to lift their voices.

A couple of weeks ago, the Supreme Court uncharacteristically reheard a case: _Louisiana v. Callais_. This has to do with a key piece of the Voting Rights Act.
Their decision on this could reshape voting rights for generations and accelerate the authoritarian capture of American democracy by weakening our representative voting power.
Many people, if they had even heard of the case, only saw it as a technical legal dispute. That is, until a new report from Fair Fight Action and Black Voters Matter Fund laid bare what’s at stake and sought to transform America’s understanding of the potential decision — exposing it for what it is, a national emergency.
They identified how the Supreme Court could gut Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and lock in 27 more safe Republican U.S. House seats, with at least 19 directly tied to the loss of its protections. **Gerrymandering would cement single-party control for a generation — the precise outcome autocrats seek — and bring about the end of free and fair elections.**
**[Now that Fair Fight Action has raised the alarm, they are mobilizing advocates across the country against this — and rallying a movement behind fair elections with fair maps. But they need our help to counter racially discriminatory gerrymandering and defend our democracy. Can you make a donation of $30 or any amount today to help Fair Fight Action keep up its vital work?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/118182863/578925285/1609117871?amount=30&refcode=bsc_emm_ffa_20251028_T1SYA_SYAonSCOTUS_v1s3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZjRmOTUzMy00OWI0LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1xel1_m0a5rvqhOcGnSjgzYUBE2GxolR-M-WDEhS6cA=)**
At the center of the Supreme Court case is Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act — the last major safeguard against racially discriminatory political maps.
For decades, Section 2 has protected communities of color from maps designed to weaken their voting power. It has been the tool by which courts have continued to dismantle Jim Crow-era tactics that persist today like splitting or “packing” Black and Brown neighborhoods to dilute their voices.
Now, the conservative justices who dominate the court are considering a radical argument: that using race to correct racial discrimination is itself unconstitutional.
This reasoning, if accepted, would gut Section 2 entirely, taking the country back to a pre-1965 reality — one where racially discriminatory maps reign unchecked and single-party rule can be locked in indefinitely, rendering Congress a mirror image of the Russian Duma.
It’s chilling — and it’s critical that groups like Fair Fight Action have the resources they need to keep identifying and calling out the consequences of these attacks. Here are just a few of the hundreds of headlines from articles drawing on Fair Fight Action and Black Voters Matter Fund’s analysis of the case:
**POLITICO:** Republicans could draw 19 more House seats after an upcoming Supreme Court ruling **NPR:** Supreme Court hears case that questions major plank of voting rights **Democracy Docket:** Fair elections — and perhaps control of Congress — at stake as SCOTUS hears challenge to VRA **USA Today:** Are Black voting rights under siege at the Supreme Court?
---
There is a path forward. It’s narrow and clear. And Fair Fight Action needs to be able to drive it forward, including:
* Continuing to raise awareness of what’s at stake — because in an autocratic takeover, the ruling regime relies on silence.
* Calling on Congress to pass pro-democracy reforms like the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.
* Contacting our local leaders and state representatives to join us in demanding passage of the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.
* Challenging all elected officials, regardless of their position, to exercise their oversight authority to hold bad actors in our courts accountable.

Patriotic Americans must act boldly to reverse the authoritarian playbook. Please make a donation today to defend our democracy alongside Fair Fight Action.

clean_body: Fair Fight Action is raising the alarm and mobilizing around solutions to this crisis of democracy. | | | Team, I founded Fair Fight Action with Lauren Groh-Wargo so a robust grassroots group would be ready to respond to attacks on our democracy — and this month has once again shown the profound need for this work. | = A couple of weeks ago, the Supreme Court uncharacteristically reheard a case: Louisiana v. Callais. This has to do with a key piece of the Voting Rights Act. Their decision on this could reshape voting rights for generations and accelerate the authoritarian capture of American democracy by weakening our representative voting power. Many people, if they had even heard of the case, only saw it as a technical legal dispute. That is, until a new report from Fair Fight Action and Black Voters Matter Fund laid bare what’s at stake and sought to transform America’s understanding of the potential decision — exposing it for what it is, a national emergency. They identified how the Supreme Court could gut Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and lock in 27 more safe Republican U.S. House seats, with at least 19 directly tied to the loss of its protections. Gerrymandering would cement single-party control for a generation — the precise outcome autocrats seek — and bring about the end of free and fair elections. = At the center of the Supreme Court case is Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act — the last major safeguard against racially discriminatory political maps. For decades, Section 2 has protected communities of color from maps designed to weaken their voting power. It has been the tool by which courts have continued to dismantle Jim Crow-era tactics that persist today like splitting or “packing” Black and Brown neighborhoods to dilute their voices. Now, the conservative justices who dominate the court are considering a radical argument: that using race to correct racial discrimination is itself unconstitutional. This reasoning, if accepted, would gut Section 2 entirely, taking the country back to a pre-1965 reality — one where racially discriminatory maps reign unchecked and single-party rule can be locked in indefinitely, rendering Congress a mirror image of the Russian Duma. It’s chilling — and it’s critical that groups like Fair Fight Action have the resources they need to keep identifying and calling out the consequences of these attacks. Here are just a few of the hundreds of headlines from articles drawing on Fair Fight Action and Black Voters Matter Fund’s analysis of the case: POLITICO: Republicans could draw 19 more House seats after an upcoming Supreme Court ruling NPR: Supreme Court hears case that questions major plank of voting rights Democracy Docket: Fair elections — and perhaps control of Congress — at stake as SCOTUS hears challenge to VRA USA Today: Are Black voting rights under siege at the Supreme Court? There is a path forward. It’s narrow and clear. And Fair Fight Action needs to be able to drive it forward, including: Continuing to raise awareness of what’s at stake — because in an autocratic takeover, the ruling regime relies on silence. Calling on Congress to pass pro-democracy reforms like the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act. Contacting our local leaders and state representatives to join us in demanding passage of the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act. Challenging all elected officials, regardless of their position, to exercise their oversight authority to hold bad actors in our courts accountable. Patriotic Americans must act boldly to reverse the authoritarian playbook. Please make a donation today to defend our democracy alongside Fair Fight Action. = Thank you, Stacey P.S.
